sentences.text: A solution is like a suitcase where you pack your agent to take it to another environment.
Every agent is created inside one: the default solution, unless you set a preferred solution.
This way your components travel together and in order, from one environment to another.
To move agents, it is best to use a custom solution with your own publisher.
Unmanaged solutions are for development, and managed solutions are for deployment.
Think of the publisher as the owner's label on the suitcase: there is only one, and it does not change inside a managed solution.
First you develop in unmanaged, then you export as managed to deploy.
Components that you add later, such as new topics or flows, must be added before you export, with Advanced and Add required objects.
Removing an agent from the solution does not remove its components.
It is an easy step to forget, and that is why it shows up on the exam.
After you import, you have to set up authentication again and publish.
And if you need to remove local changes from a managed agent, use Solution Layers and Remove unmanaged layer.
These are the two steps that finish the solution's trip between environments and clean up anything local.
If it will not export, look for a topic with dots in its name.
And you cannot change the publisher of a component in a managed solution.
These are small details, but they appear a lot in the questions on this topic.
